{{Short description|Mathematical theorem in complex analysis}}
'''Cartwright's theorem''' is a mathematical [[theorem]] in [[complex analysis]], discovered by the British mathematician [[Mary Cartwright]]. It gives an estimate of the maximum [[Absolute value|modulus]] of an [[analytical function]] when the unit [[disc (functional analysis)|disc]] takes the same value no more than ''p'' times.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Liu |first1=H. C. |last2=Macintyre |first2=A. J. |date= |title=CARTWRIGHT'S THEOREM ON FUNCTIONS BOUNDED AT THE INTEGERS |url=https://www.ams.org/journals/proc/1961-012-03/S0002-9939-1961-0125222-4/S0002-9939-1961-0125222-4.pdf |journal=American Mathematical Society |doi=}}</ref>

== Statement ==
Cartwright's theorem says that, for every integer <math>p \ge 1</math>, there exists a constant <math>C_p</math> such that for every <math>p</math>-valent [[holomorphic function]] <math>f(z) = \sum_{i=0}^\infty a_n z^n</math> in disc <math>|z| < 1</math>, we have the bound
:<math>|f(z)| \leq \frac{\max_{0 \leq i \leq p}|a_i|}{(1-r)^{2p}} C_p</math>
in an absolute value for all <math>z</math> in the disc <math>|z| \leq r</math> and <math>r \leq 1</math>.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Blank |first1=Natalia |last2=Ulanovskii |first2=Alexander |title=On Cartwright's theorem |date=October 2016 |url=https://www.ams.org/journals/proc/2016-144-10/S0002-9939-2016-13200-0/S0002-9939-2016-13200-0.pdf |journal=Proceedings of the American Mathematical Society |volume=144 |issue=10 |pages=4221–4230|doi=10.1090/proc/13200 |s2cid=119148466 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last1=McMurran |first1=Shawnee |last2=Tattersall |first2=James |title=Mary Cartwright |url=https://www.ams.org/notices/199902/mem-cartwright.pdf |website=American Mathematical Society}}</ref>
